text:
tia: Heads up  seeing a persistent uptick in pcie_uncorrectable on usw1 rack C5. A couple of multi-tenant pods show 95th latency rising. Might be a noisy workload thrashing HBM. thinking a focused throttle + reserve routing fallback.

harry: Yep dashboards match. HBM_evictions spiked ~2x in last 8m. Which nodes?

tia: Shortlist: usw1-c5-03, usw1-c5-07, usw1-c5-11. I can mark them no-new-alloc and run a slow cordon if needed. Avoid draining more than 2 at once.

nick: Throttle first pls. We lost a lot of warm cache last week when we mass-drained. Suggest: set per-alloc concurrency_limit=0.6 for 4m and reduce batch_size at the serving layer.

ravi: For dedicated tenants we should not cross-region. But dev tenants can failover to eu-west1 reserve slices. Cost hit estimate: ~10% extra token spend for egress+vm for that traffic. Keep TTL 20m.

tia: Ops runbook?

harry: ops-bot:open runbook gpu-noisy-3 -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-noisy-3. It has staggered drain sequence and routing fallback snippet. Notifying oncall.

ops-bot: runbook opened (gpu-noisy-3). oncall: harry_sre pinged. routing patch id: 6960003000 queued.

nick: Drain plan if throttle fails: (1) annotate node with "no-warmup: true", (2) cordon then drain non-dedicated pods with 2m grace, stagger 3 nodes per 10m window.

tia: kubectl commands I'll run: ```
kubectl annotate node <node> infra/no-warmup=true
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=8m
```

harry: Also ensure autoscaler profiles include "preserve-warm-pool" check to avoid scale-to-zero. Preflight that first.

ravi: If pcie_err persists after two throttle cycles -> enable serving-mode=cache-only for affected allocs and switch heavy models to v2-q6 (lower mem) for dev tenants. Notify model owners.

tia: Doing throttle now: per-alloc rate_limit -> 60% of baseline for 5m. I'll post metrics in 2m.

ops-bot: throttle applied to allocations: alloc-8345, alloc-8349, alloc-8358. Observability trace started: trace-6960002222.

harry: Quick check: any dedicated reservations on the shortlist nodes?

tia: c5-11 has one dedicated reserved slice (tenant: acme_corp). We'll avoid moving that node unless absolutely needed. Focus on c5-03 and c5-07 first.

nick: Good. If we move dev traffic to eu-west1, route service might spin up cold lanes. Consider pre-warming reserve slices by placing a small synthetic warmup (no-op) to keep KV warm. But that trades cost. Tradeoff decision?

ravi: Pre-warm small (<1% traffic) for 5m before flipping major weight. Cost <0.5% overall, reduces cold-start spike. OK to do for this mitigation window.

tia: Update: pcie_uncorrectable dropped ~38% after 90s of throttle. Tail latency down ~25%. Holding off on drain.

harry: Great. Keep throttle running and monitor for 10m. If trend reverses, escalate to node drain plan.

nick: Follow-up items: add noisy-alloc auto-throttle rule (threshold-based) and add a scheduler preference hint for io-heavy pods to prefer reserve slices. Opened infra#1834.

ravi: I'll capture cost delta for the cross-region fallback and add a TTL enforcement in routing-service so it auto-rolls back after 20m.

tia: Preflight autoscaler: confirmed respects infra/no-warmup annotation. Safe to cordon if needed.

ops-bot: oncall: harry_sre acknowledged. routing-service patch queued (6960003000).

tia: OK folks, re-eval in 10m. For now: throttle active, drains on standby, reserve lanes pre-warm queued. Thanks.

harry: Note for postmortem: we should record which model family induced the HBM churn and feed that into Optimize recommendations.

nick: +1. Also log the exact pcie_err signature so we can detect similar patterns earlier.

ravi: Filed follow-up: infra#1834 (auto-throttle + scheduler-hint) and infra#1835 (reserve-slice prewarm TTL). Closing this thread to move to runbook channel.
